sections.title: 60.2 Deployment components
sections.body:
| Component | Deployment approach |
|--------|--------|
| API gateway | Stateless replicas |
| Agent runtime | Independently scalable workers |
| Human approval service | Durable authenticated API |
| Checkpoint storage | Persistent replicated database |
| Model services | Approved provider or isolated inference deployment |
| Tool gateway | Restricted network and credentials |
| Telemetry collector | Protected ingestion endpoint |
| Evaluation workers | Separate capacity from production agents |
sections.visualSummary: This diagram walks through “Component Deployment approach -------- -------- API gateway Stateless re” one stage at a time.

steps.label: Load
steps.narration: Loading converts PDFs, DOCX, CSV, HTML and other sources into a consistent document object with text plus metadata.

steps.label: Clean
steps.narration: Cleaning removes boilerplate, normalizes unicode, strips headers/footers, and prepares text so chunking and embeddings stay high quality.

steps.label: Chunk
steps.narration: Chunking splits documents into retrieval units. Size and overlap control whether evidence is complete enough without adding noise.

steps.label: Embed
steps.narration: Embedding turns each chunk into a dense vector so semantically similar questions and passages can be matched.

steps.label: Index
steps.narration: Indexing stores vectors (and often sparse signals) for fast nearest-neighbor search with filters for tenant, source, or time.

steps.label: Retrieve
steps.narration: Retrieval finds the Top-K chunks for a query using dense, sparse, or hybrid search before generation.

steps.label: Generate
steps.narration: Generation builds an answer from the retrieved context. Good prompts require evidence, citations, and abstention when support is weak.

sections.title: 60.3 Kubernetes production considerations
sections.body:
For agent workers, configure resource requests and limits, readiness and liveness probes, graceful shutdown and an appropriate termination grace period.

Scale according to queue age, outstanding tasks and dependency capacity rather than CPU utilization alone.

A worker receiving a termination signal should stop accepting new tasks, persist safe progress and release or expire its lease appropriately.

Do not automatically mark every interrupted external operation as failed.

sections.title: 60.4 CI/CD release pipeline
sections.body:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Code and configuration] --> B[Unit and contract tests]
    B --> C[Agent evaluation]
    C --> D[Security regression]
    D --> E[Load and resilience tests]
    E --> F[Shadow or canary release]
    F --> G{Release gates satisfied?}
    G -->|Yes| H[Promote]
    G -->|No| I[Rollback or disable]
```

Agent deployments must version prompts, tools, skills, policies, memory schemas, model settings and graph definitions in addition to source code.

- Scale according to queue age, outstanding tasks and dependency capacity rather than CPU utilization alone.
- A worker receiving a termination signal should stop accepting new tasks, persist safe progress and release or expire its lease appropriately.
- Do not automatically mark every interrupted external operation as failed.

quiz.question: What is the most production-ready mindset for "Part — 60. Production deployment architecture"?
options: Trust fluent model output without checks
Define detect → mitigate → validate loops around the concept
Only optimize prompts and ignore systems design
quiz.explanation: Production GenAI systems need explicit detection, mitigation, and validation around every critical concept.
